intent: One dot per item, placed by two numeric measures, like accounts by monthly revenue and support tickets. Optional groups by colour and dot size by a third value.
useWhen: The relationship between two numeric measures across many items, like revenue against tickets per account
Spotting clusters, outliers and items that break the pattern
Comparing groups of items on the same two measures, like plans or regions
doNotUseWhen: Comparing amounts across categories — use BarChart
A short ranking by one measure — use BarList
Part of a whole — use PieChart

label.note: What the dot is, like an account name. Shown in the tooltip, the table and the dot's accessible name.

group.note: Colours the dot by group, --chart-1 to --chart-6 in order of first appearance, and adds a legend when there are two or more groups.

size.note: The third value, read when size is value. Zero or more.

data.note: One row per item. Rows without a finite x and y are left out.

xLabel.note: Names the horizontal measure, like Monthly revenue. Shown under the x axis, in the tooltip and the table.

yLabel.note: Names the vertical measure, like Support tickets. Shown above the y axis, in the tooltip and the table.

size.note: fixed draws every dot the same size. value sizes each dot by its size field, by area (square root), so a dot with four times the value has twice the width.

sizeLabel.note: Names the size value in the tooltip and the table, like Seats. Only used with size value.

x.note: (value: number) => string for x values and the x axis.

y.note: (value: number) => string for y values and the y axis.

valueFormatter.note: Each defaults to the chart format: 1,240, 12.4k, 1.2M on axes, the full value in the tooltip and table.

title.note: Chart heading on the frame, like the other charts. Also names the plot for screen readers.

actions.note: Kit Buttons in the chart header, before the Table toggle, like an icon-only Ask. ghost sm reads quietest. Setting it draws the frame even with no title.

requirements: Title on the figure when provided, and the plot is a role=group named by it
The dots are one Tab stop; arrow keys move between them in x order (then y), Home and End go to the first and last
Each dot names its label, both measures, the size when set and the group
The tooltip shows on focus as well as on hover, and the focused dot gets a visible ring
Colour is never the only cue for a group: the legend, tooltip and table name it
The Table toggle swaps the chart for a plain table with every value

doNot: Do not use it for change over time — use LineChart
Do not use it to compare categories — use BarChart
Do not join the dots with lines; order along x is not a sequence
Do not use status colours for groups; a group that means good or bad says so in its name
Do not use more than six groups; the chart palette has six colours
Do not use raw hex or primitive --color-* ramps
Do not wrap a chart in a Card only to get a header button — pass actions
snippet:
<ScatterChart
  title="Accounts by revenue and tickets"
  xLabel="Monthly revenue"
  yLabel="Support tickets"
  data={[
    { id: "acme", label: "Acme", x: 12400, y: 18, group: "Pro" },
    { id: "globex", label: "Globex", x: 31800, y: 42, group: "Enterprise" },
    { id: "initech", label: "Initech", x: 4200, y: 9, group: "Pro" },
  ]}
/>
